tasks.title: Fix test project infrastructure
tasks.description:
The test project has two blocking issues that must be resolved before any real tests can run.

**1. ProjectReference path bug:** In `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests.csproj`, the path `../src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj` is wrong. From `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/`, `../` goes to `tests/` not the repo root. The correct path is `../../src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj`.

**2. TFM mismatch:** Tests target `net8.0` but only the .NET 10 runtime is available on this machine (`dotnet test` aborts with 'framework not found'). Change the test project TFM to `net10.0`.

**3. Add Moq and System.Net.Http:** Add `<PackageReference Include="Moq" Version="4.20.72" />` and `<PackageReference Include="System.Net.Http" Version="4.3.4" />` (or use the built-in HttpClient from net10.0 — just Moq is sufficient) so HTTP handler mocking is available for later tasks.

**4. Add InternalsVisibleTo:** In the driver project, add `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` containing `[assembly: System.Runtime.CompilerServices.InternalsVisibleTo("LinqPad.Databricks.Tests")]` so internal constructors on HTTP clients can be called from tests.

**Acceptance:** `dotnet build LinqPad.Databricks.sln` with 0 errors and 0 warnings; `dotnet test LinqPad.Databricks.sln` runs and passes all current smoke tests.

tasks.title: Implement Databricks HTTP base client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Http/DatabricksHttpClient.cs` — a reusable HTTP client wrapping `HttpClient` for all Databricks REST calls.

**Responsibilities:**
- Constructor `DatabricksHttpClient(string workspaceUrl, string pat)` — validates URL (regex `^https://[a-zA-Z0-9\-\.]+(\.(azuredatabricks\.net|databricks\.azure\.cn))/?$`), stores PAT.
- Internal/test constructor `DatabricksHttpClient(string workspaceUrl, string pat, HttpMessageHandler handler)` for injection of mock handlers.
- `GetAsync<T>(string path, CancellationToken ct)` and `PostAsync<T>(string path, object body, CancellationToken ct)` helpers: set `Authorization: Bearer <pat>` header, serialize/deserialize JSON with `System.Text.Json` (`JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true }`).
- On non-2xx response: read body, parse `{ "message": ... }` or `{ "error": ... }` field, throw a custom `DatabricksApiException(string message, string? errorCode, int statusCode)` that extends `Exception`.
- Expose `DatabricksApiException` as a public class in `Http/DatabricksApiException.cs`.

**JSON models needed now (add a `Models/` folder):**
- `PagedResponse<T>` with `Items: List<T>` and `NextPageToken: string?`.

**Acceptance:** Unit test with a `MockHttpMessageHandler` (manual `DelegatingHandler` subclass or Moq) can construct `DatabricksHttpClient` via the internal 3-arg constructor, perform a GET, and receive a deserialized object; also verify that a 4xx response throws `DatabricksApiException` with the parsed message.

tasks.title: Implement Unity Catalog REST client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Catalog/UnityCatalogClient.cs` using `DatabricksHttpClient`.

**Note:** `PagedResponse<T>` already exists at `Models/PagedResponse.cs` — do not recreate it.

**Models** (add to `Models/` or `Catalog/`):
- `CatalogInfo { string Name; string? Comment; }` — JSON property names: `name`, `comment`.
- `SchemaInfo { string Name; string CatalogName; string? Comment; }` — JSON: `name`, `catalog_name`, `comment`.
- `TableInfo { string Name; string SchemaName; string CatalogName; string TableType; string? Comment; }` — JSON: `name`, `schema_name`, `catalog_name`, `table_type`, `comment`. TableType values: `MANAGED`, `EXTERNAL`, `VIEW`, `MATERIALIZED_VIEW`.

API responses use `{ "catalogs": [...], "next_page_token": "..." }` for catalogs, `{ "schemas": [...] }` for schemas, `{ "tables": [...] }` for tables — NOT a generic `items` field. Model accordingly (separate paged-response wrappers or concrete response classes).

**Methods on `UnityCatalogClient`:**
- Constructor: `UnityCatalogClient(DatabricksHttpClient http)`.
- `ListCatalogsAsync(CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<CatalogInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/catalogs`, paginate via `next_page_token` by appending `?page_token={token}` on subsequent requests.
- `ListSchemasAsync(string catalogName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<SchemaInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/schemas?catalog_name={catalogName}`, paginate.
- `ListTablesAsync(string catalogName, string schemaName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<TableInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/tables?catalog_name={catalogName}&schema_name={schemaName}`, paginate.

**Acceptance:** Unit tests in `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/UnityCatalogClientTests.cs` using the existing `FakeHandler : DelegatingHandler` pattern: (a) `ListCatalogsAsync` single-page returns correct items; (b) multi-page (two responses with `next_page_token`) returns combined list; (c) `ListTablesAsync` passes both query params; (d) 403 response propagates as `DatabricksApiException`. `dotnet test` passes all tests.

tasks.title: Add column details to Schema Explorer
tasks.description:
Currently tables and views in the Schema Explorer show no column children. Add column-level ExplorerItems under each table/view so users can see field names and types without running a query.

**Implementation:**
1. Add `ColumnInfo` model in `Catalog/ColumnInfo.cs` with `name` (string), `type_name` (string), `comment` (string?), `nullable` (bool?) JSON-deserialized fields.
2. Extend `TableInfo` model with a `Columns` list property (populated by the detail endpoint, not the list endpoint).
3. Add `GetTableAsync(string catalogName, string schemaName, string tableName, CancellationToken ct)` method to `UnityCatalogClient` that calls `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/tables/{catalog_name}.{schema_name}.{table_name}` and returns a `TableInfo` with columns populated.
4. In `DatabricksDriver.GetSchemaAndBuildAssembly`, after adding each `tblItem`, call `GetTableAsync` to fetch columns. For each column, add a child `ExplorerItem` with `ExplorerItemKind.FieldOrProperty`, `ExplorerIcon.Blank`, and the column type appended to the name (e.g. `"id (LONG)"`). Wrap in try/catch to avoid failing the whole tree if one table detail call fails.
5. Performance note: fetching columns for every table may be slow on large workspaces. Tolerate this for MVP; a future task can add lazy/on-demand loading.

**Tests:** Add `UnityCatalogClientTests` cases for `GetTableAsync` using the `QueuedFakeHandler` pattern. Verify columns are deserialized and returned correctly. Verify `DatabricksDriver` (or integration smoke) that tblItem children are populated.

**Acceptance criteria:** A table ExplorerItem has child items for each column with name and type. Test for `GetTableAsync` passes with mocked HTTP.

tasks.title: Replace ADO facade smoke tests with real tests
tasks.description:
DatabricksTests.cs and DriverStubTests.cs currently contain only trivial smoke assertions (`Assert.True(true)`) that provide no coverage. Replace them with meaningful unit tests for the ADO facade layer.

**Implementation:**
1. In `DatabricksTests.cs`, replace the smoke test class with `DatabricksConnectionTests` covering:
   - `Open()` sets `State = ConnectionState.Open` and creates `ExecutionClient`.
   - `Close()` sets `State = ConnectionState.Closed` and nulls `ExecutionClient`.
   - Double-`Open()` is idempotent.
   - `ConnectionString` getter returns expected format.
2. In `DriverStubTests.cs`, replace the smoke test class with `DatabricksCommandTests` covering:
   - `ExecuteNonQuery()` returns row count from `ExecutionClient` result.
   - `ExecuteScalar()` returns first cell value (or `null` for empty result).
   - `ExecuteDbDataReader()` returns a `DbDataReader` with correct column count and row count.
   - `ExecuteInternal()` auto-opens the connection if not already open.
3. Use the `QueuedFakeHandler` / `DatabricksHttpClient` internal constructor pattern already established in the test project to construct a `DatabricksConnection` wired to fake HTTP, then attach a `DatabricksCommand` and verify behavior.
4. Add a helper method in the test project to build a `DatabricksConnection` backed by a `QueuedFakeHandler` for a given set of canned responses (avoids duplication).

**Acceptance criteria:** All previously-failing or trivial tests are replaced; `dotnet test` still passes with >= 25 tests total. Each new test covers a distinct code path.
